title: Multiple authentication failures followed by a success. - j.mehta on fin-app-01
severity_rationale: Rubric: critical = success after brute force (>= 10 failures) AND sudo / new account after the login on a high-criticality host. All conditions met: 50 failures from external IP, sudo to root at 09:44:03, new account backup_svc at 09:46:11, fin-app-01 is criticality high and internet-exposed. Severity could not be lower than critical per rubric order.
confidence_rationale: All key evidence available: 50 failures from Wazuh, success after failures, source IP external to baseline, IP reputation malicious (MOCK intel), sudo and account change after login, host context, account baseline check. No gaps or conflicts in the evidence chain. (MOCK intel) Some uncertainty remains from incomplete tshark coverage of post-login sessions, which prevents full confirmation of no outbound connections.

executive_summary.text: On 2026-11-18, a brute-force SSH attack was detected targeting account j.mehta on the critical finance application server fin-app-01. Over a 10-minute window (09:31:02-09:41:55), 50 authentication failures were logged from external IP 203.0.113.77 (MOCK intel). A successful login occurred at 09:42:17.512Z, after which the account executed sudo to root at 09:44:03. Just two minutes later, at 09:46:11, a new local account backup_svc was created on the same host. Threat intelligence indicates 203.0.113.77 is malicious (reputation score 92; categories: ssh-bruteforce, password-spraying, scanner) (MOCK intel). The combination of external brute force, privileged escalation, and unauthorized account creation on a high-criticality internet-exposed host constitutes a critical-severity incident. j.mehta's account is presumed compromised.
